overview_markdown:
SmallClaw is a local-first AI agent framework built in TypeScript, designed specifically to work well with small local models via Ollama, llama.cpp, and LM Studio, with optional hybrid support for OpenAI API and Codex OAuth. It provides a chat-first web UI where the agent gets real tools: file operations with line-level edits, multi-provider web search (Tavily, Google, Brave, DuckDuckGo), Playwright-powered browser automation, terminal access, persistent session memory, and a drop-in SKILL.md skills system.

Its key architectural differentiator is a single-pass chat handler: one LLM call decides whether to respond conversationally or invoke tools, avoiding the separate planning/execution/verification agent loops that small models handle poorly. This reduces latency and cost compared to heavier multi-agent frameworks. Recent commits show active development including a v1.1 system overhaul, security hardening, Docker improvements, background tasks, sub-agents, and a Telegram file browser.

Compared to OpenClaw, SmallClaw trades ecosystem breadth for simplicity and small-model efficiency. However, its licensing is unclear (the description asserts 'All rights reserved' while the README links a LICENSE file), there are no formal GitHub releases, and community traction is modest at 259 stars. It is best suited for individual users who want a free, private, local assistant without OpenClaw's operational complexity.
